output.body: Take a different function: sum_to(n) equals 1+2+...+n, written as sum_to(n) = n + sum_to(n-1). Called on 3, it asks for sum_to(2), then sum_to(1), then sum_to(0), and without a rule for the smallest input it would keep going to sum_to(-1) and beyond. So we add the line 'if n is 0, give 0 and make no further call', and that is where the chain of calls ends.
output.key_idea: A recursive function stops when some input is handled directly, without calling itself, and every recursive call moves toward that input.
